headline: Scientists in Buenos Aires used a computer to recreate a sparrow song last heard in the 1960s, and within three months a local bird began copying parts of it.
score_reason: Pool score 5 lowered by 1: The Guardian reported it on 13 Oct, and the AI link is only a future possibility.
importance_line: Conservationists may one day tutor birds of dwindling species with synthetic song, but this is one sparrow species that is not considered globally vulnerable, and AI tutoring is only a possibility.
summary: The Guardian reports that physicist Gabriel Mindlin of the University of Buenos Aires and colleagues rebuilt a rufous-collared sparrow song from hand-drawn 1960s notes, and less than three months after they played it in a park that had lost it, a local bird began copying parts of it. Researchers hope synthetic recordings could help teach songs to birds of declining species, and the paper adds that AI might provide live tutoring in future.
notes: The Times of India page returned no text; entry built from The Guardian's report on the same study.
